content: {"summary":"Two waves of AUTH‑E401X errors occurred: the first when the first new auth‑service pod became Ready at 14:08, and the second after the rollback when the first old‑version pod returned at 14:23, each caused by incompatible session encoding between versions.","likely_cause":"The new release changed the encoding of session values in Redis, making old and new pods unable to read each other's sessions, which produced two logout waves.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"First wave triggered when the first new pod became Ready at 14:08","evidence_ids":["RB-026#4"],"quote":"At 14:08, as the first new pod became Ready, `AUTH‑E401X` jumped"},{"text":"Second wave triggered after rollback when the first old‑version pod returned at 14:23, logging out users logged in since 14:08","evidence_ids":["RB-026#4"],"quote":"From 14:23, as the first old‑version pod returned, everyone who had logged in since 14:08 was logged out"},{"text":"Root cause is incompatible session encoding between old and new versions, causing errors in both directions","evidence_ids":["RB-026#4","RB-026#3"],"quote":"new pods couldn't decode sessions written by old pods, and the reverse"}],"next_checks":["Check auth‑service logs for AUTH‑E401X counts per pod around 14:08 and 14:23","Verify the commit that changed session encoding in July 2026","Confirm Redis primary remained unchanged during the incident","Review rollout configuration to ensure only one pod updates at a time"]}
